title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the values of its nodes grouped level by level, but alternating direction: the first level left-to-right, the next right-to-left, and so on, zigzagging back and forth.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to implement the zigzag grouping.

examples.explanation: Level 0 reads left-to-right (3). Level 1 reads right-to-left (20,9). Level 2 reads left-to-right again (15,7).
An empty tree has no levels at all, so the result is an empty list.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 2000]
hints: Start with standard level-order BFS, collecting each level's values into a list exactly like normal level order traversal.
The only difference from plain level order is that every other level needs to be reversed before being added to the result.
Keep a boolean flag that flips after every level; when it indicates a 'reverse' level, reverse that level's list before appending it to the result.

solution.approach: Perform standard BFS level order traversal, collecting each level's values left-to-right using the queue as usual. Track a flag that toggles after every level; whenever the flag indicates the current level should be reversed, reverse the level's list before appending it to the result. This is simpler and avoids needing a deque with alternating push directions.
